sections.html:
You can hire an agent, go private or take a cash offer. Frankfort adds local rules that many Kentucky towns lack: a rental inspection before any new tenant moves in, short-term rental caps in the historic districts, and floodplain permits along the Kentucky River.

Frankfort is the state capital and the Franklin County seat. It had 28,602 residents in 2020 and is estimated at 28,657 as of July 1, 2025, so the market is steady rather than growing. Owners live in 48.8% of homes, which means renters edge out owners. A typical owner-held house is valued at $183,700, median gross rent is $944, and median household income is $53,073. The city has 12,906 households averaging 2.11 people. Government jobs make up a big part of local work.

The Kentucky River makes an S-turn through the middle of town and splits it into Downtown, South Frankfort, the small Bellepoint neighborhood and the suburban West Side and East Side. Interstate 64 runs beside the city and Interstate 75 is nearby. Commercial flights leave from Blue Grass Airport in Lexington, since Frankfort's Capital City Airport handles general and military aviation.

Owners deal with two collectors. The city's Finance Office bills the city tax and the Frankfort Independent Schools tax, and the Franklin County Sheriff's Office, at 974 River Bend Road, publishes the county tax bills. The Franklin County PVA values property at 100% of fair market value on each January 1.

Frankfort city tax: dates and penalty
DateWhat happens to the city bill
By November 1Bills available
Before November 302% discount for payment received
By December 31Bill due
After the due date10% penalty plus interest, if received or postmarked late

The Finance Office answers questions at 502-875-8500, and bills can be searched and paid online. Mortgage escrow accounts pay from the bill the servicer receives, so give your lender the tax bill promptly. Address changes go through the Franklin County PVA.

sections.h2: Which school district is a house in?
sections.html:
Two public districts cover the city. Frankfort Independent Schools serves the downtown neighborhoods, including Downtown, South Frankfort, Bellepoint and Tanglewood. Franklin County Public Schools covers the remainder of the city and county, with Franklin County High School and Western Hills High School among its campuses.

The split affects tax as well as schooling, because the city's Finance Office bills the Frankfort Independent Schools tax along with the city tax. Check which district a house falls in before you describe it to a buyer.

The river has flooded the city many times, with the highest recorded floods in 1937 and 1978. A levee on the North Frankfort side was finished in 1969 and a floodwall protects South Frankfort. Construction or remodeling inside the floodplain goes through extra review.

  • Planning and Community Development serves as the floodplain coordinator for the city.
  • Building in the floodplain needs a local Floodplain Development Permit, plus a stream permit from the state Division of Water where one applies.
  • Reviewers use Flood Elevation Certificates signed by a surveyor, engineer or architect.
  • The city's Community Rating System status saves property owners 10% on flood insurance premiums.

For a house near the river, find out whether an elevation certificate exists for the address, and hold onto flood insurance papers for the buyer.

Frankfort requires a rental inspection before any new tenant takes possession, however long the previous tenant stayed. The standard fee is $20, and it rises to $100 when a unit has no current inspection. Staff usually book the inspection for the following business day, between 8:00 and 4:30, with the owner or an agent on site.

The city does not enforce Kentucky's landlord and tenant act, but its staff will help with health and safety problems that were not present before occupancy or that went uncorrected. Planning and Building answers at 502-352-2094. Short-term rentals sit under separate rules set by ordinance in December 2024.

  • An annual $250 license fee for every short-term rental unit.
  • Non-owner-occupied rentals are conditional uses in the Special Capital and Special Historic districts, capped at 5% of dwelling units in the first and 8 rentals in the second.
  • A $100 first citation, then $25 for each further day, and license revocation if the violation continues.

A house that has served as a rental should come with its inspection and registration papers.

sections.h2: What a Frankfort seller pays at closing
sections.html:
KRS 142.050 sets the seller's deed tax at $0.50 per $500 block of value. The Franklin County Clerk takes it at recording. The mortgage payoff, any lien release and the seller's part of the year's tax come on top. Agent fees apply only if you list with one, and repair costs fall on whoever agrees to take them on in the contract.

A cash buyer can shorten this list. The house is bought as it stands, no lender has to approve it, and the payoff and tax are paid from the sale money at the table. Ask the title company for a settlement statement a few days ahead.

Closing is held at a title company or an attorney's office. You sign the deed, the closing agent pays off your mortgage and any open tax from your proceeds, and the clerk records the deed. Bring a photo ID and your keys. If the house was inherited, the title company needs to see who has authority to sign before it will close, so have the estate papers ready.

If the buyer is paying cash, there is no lender to wait on and no appraisal to clear. That can bring a closing within days instead of weeks, as long as the title search is clean and both tax bills are settled.

• Pull both tax bills, city and county, and confirm each is paid.
  • Find out whether an elevation certificate or flood insurance policy exists for the address.
  • Gather the rental inspection and short-term rental registration papers if the house has been rented.
  • Ask Planning and Building about open permits or violations.
  • Get a mortgage payoff letter dated close to the closing day.

Handing these to the buyer's side up front keeps a state-capital sale from stalling on small questions.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax on a Frankfort house?
faqs.a: City Finance bills the city and Frankfort Independent Schools taxes, and the Franklin County Sheriff's Office publishes the county bills. Call 502-875-8500 if the district on your bill is unclear.

faqs.q: When is the city of Frankfort's property tax due?
faqs.a: The bills are available by November 1 and due by December 31, and payments received before November 30 get a 2% discount. After the due date a 10% penalty plus interest applies.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required before a Frankfort tenant moves in?
faqs.a: Yes. A rental inspection is required before any new tenant takes possession, and the fee is $20, or $100 if the unit has no current inspection. Call Planning and Building at 502-352-2094 to schedule it.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Frankfort?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. Each unit pays a $250 annual license fee, and non-owner-occupied rentals in the Special Capital and Special Historic districts are conditional uses with caps. Owner-occupied rentals must meet the ordinance's standards for stay length, occupancy and parking.

faqs.q: Does floodplain location matter when selling in Frankfort?
faqs.a: It changes what you can build or remodel, because construction there needs a local Floodplain Development Permit and elevation certificate review. Planning and Community Development can say whether one is on file for your address.
